_comment: Guided tour of the emtk burst-MLE app. Targets are keys the app records: add_files, detector, auto, window_start, decay, toolAction_run, distribution. The Auto and Fit steps wait for the real press.

steps.title: One lifetime per burst
steps.text:
A burst holds a few hundred photons, so its decay is sparse. This tool fits one lifetime per burst and detector by Poisson maximum likelihood, with the IRF and background held fixed.

Every window shows what the engine computed; with no fit they say so and draw nothing.

steps.title: Generate demonstration photons
steps.text: Generate 16 synthetic bursts of 1000 photons each. The input lifetime is 2 ns; fitted estimates fluctuate. This replaces current working inputs. Fitting is still your next action.

steps.title: Choose the tttrlib model
steps.text: Fit23 estimates one lifetime with polarization. Fit24 estimates a two-lifetime mixture. Fit25 chooses among four fixed lifetime candidates. Select Fit24 or Fit25 to see its parameter rows, then select Fit23 for this single-lifetime demo.

steps.title: Burst runs
steps.text: The Input section lists the burst runs in the workspace: the runs of the measurement containers, each under its photon stream in the Datasets view. Select one or more and press Use selected; Open in… on a Datasets row, or dragging rows onto this tool, does the same. Files dropped on the ChiSurf window are added to the workspace.

steps.title: Detectors
steps.text: The detectors (routing channels per colour) come from the Detector setup tab, the same editor the other tools use. Pick the one to fit here.

steps.title: IRF and background
steps.text: The fit needs an IRF and a background. Auto IRF/background picks the binning and the fit window, estimates a Gaussian IRF and the background from the photons outside the bursts, and fits. A measured IRF and background give better lifetimes.

steps.title: Where the IRF comes from
steps.text:
The IRF tab has one choice, IRF from. Leave it on Auto: it takes the reference dye of Data Selection, else the IRF measurement, else the photons outside the bursts, else an estimate from the data. A source that was not measured is greyed.

IRF tool opens the IRF in the IRF Estimation tool; what you estimate there comes back here and is fitted.

steps.title: A measured IRF and background
steps.text: A measured IRF (scatter or a short-lifetime reference) and a sample-free background are better than the estimate. Open the IRF/BG files tab: the Measured IRF and Measured background sections list the photon streams in the workspace — select the measurement and press Use selected. With one for all the files serve every detector. IRF model chooses the shape Auto IRF/background estimates.

steps.title: The fit window
steps.text: The window is the range of micro-time bins that enter the likelihood. Leave out the empty bins before the prompt and the noisy tail. A change refits the current decay.

steps.title: Optimise the settings
steps.text: Opt searches the VH shift, the sub-bin shifts, the IRF window and the IRF thresholds for the lowest 2I* of this decay (the number of fits is Opt iterations in the IRF tab) and applies the best; it is never worse than what you had. Save fit keeps the settings on the selected detector setup.

steps.title: Read the fit
steps.text: The model should follow the data across the fit window. The editable Fit parameters table shows the selected model's starts, fixed flags and results. Fit25 lifetimes remain candidates; its winning index is reported separately.

steps.title: Fit the bursts
steps.text: Fits every burst of every file and detector in worker processes. The histogram then shows the lifetimes of all bursts and the table their medians.

steps.title: The lifetimes
steps.text: Bursts fitted, median and mean lifetime of each detector. Each burst's lifetime goes into the burst table: plot its distribution in ndX, where it can be gated. A single burst's lifetime is noisy: read the distribution, not one value.
